data.sql:
-- stg_orders: cleaned order stream.
-- Excludes cancelled and refunded orders from the revenue path.
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE staging.stg_orders AS
SELECT
    order_id,
    CAST(order_ts AS TIMESTAMP) AS order_ts,
    CAST(CAST(order_ts AS TIMESTAMP) AS DATE) AS order_day,
    customer_id,
    currency,
    CAST(amount AS DOUBLE) AS amount,
    payment_processor,
    status
FROM raw.raw_orders
WHERE status NOT IN ('cancelled', 'refunded');

-- fct_revenue: daily revenue fact, USD-normalized via stg_fx_rates.
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE marts.fct_revenue AS
SELECT
    o.order_day AS day,
    COUNT(*) AS order_count,
    ROUND(SUM(o.amount * fx.usd_rate), 2) AS revenue_usd,
    ROUND(AVG(o.amount * fx.usd_rate), 2) AS aov_usd,
    ROUND(MEDIAN(o.amount * fx.usd_rate), 2) AS aov_median_usd
FROM staging.stg_orders o
JOIN staging.stg_fx_rates fx
  ON fx.rate_day = o.order_day
 AND fx.currency = o.currency
GROUP BY o.order_day
ORDER BY o.order_day;

root_cause.summary: The new cloudpay_v2 payment provider, cut over on 2026-08-07, reports raw.raw_orders.amount in minor units (cents) instead of the contracted major currency units — silently multiplying executive revenue by exactly 100x.
root_cause.detail:
SYMPTOM: marts.exec_revenue_metric.revenue = 2,737,323.50 for kpi_day 2026-08-09 vs expected 29,349.39 (anomaly_ratio 93.3). Baseline comparison shows a step change with onset exactly 2026-08-07: revenue_ratio 100.0 / 100.0 / 99.99 on 08-07, 08-08, 08-09, while 07-31..08-06 sit at ratio 1.0 [ev_99f62985f4, ev_ac73812134].

NOT A VOLUME EVENT: order_count is identical to baseline on all three affected days (334/349/327 vs 334/349/327). The entire distortion is per-order: aov_median_usd inflated 100x (6483.50 vs 64.84; 5972.00 vs 59.72; 6213.00 vs 62.13) [ev_99f62985f4].

LINEAGE: DataHub column-level lineage gives a single path raw.raw_orders.amount -> staging.stg_orders.amount -> marts.fct_revenue.revenue_usd -> marts.exec_revenue_metric.revenue, with the only other contributing branch being stg_fx_rates.usd_rate [ev_8659030b83].

FX BRANCH ELIMINATED: usd_rate is stable and in-range across the onset window (CAD 0.717928-0.719844, EUR 1.070478-1.079818, GBP 1.26956-1.27464) — no 100x scaling [ev_66422a90c1].

TRANSFORMS ELIMINATED AS ORIGIN: stg_orders.sql merely CASTs amount to DOUBLE and filters cancelled/refunded [ev_07ca87974f]; fct_revenue.sql only computes SUM/AVG/MEDIAN of amount * usd_rate [ev_143dc8d308]. Neither contains a scaling factor, so the 100x is already present in the raw feed.

ORIGIN ISOLATED BY COHORT: profiling raw.raw_orders.amount segmented by payment_processor shows a complete provider cutover on 2026-08-07. Through 08-06, orders come from legacy_pos and shopgate with mean ~79-86 and median ~60-70. From 08-07 onward, 100% of orders come from a new processor cloudpay_v2 with mean 7873-8239, median 5955-6374, max up to 55262 [ev_46ed4fc52d]. Every single cloudpay_v2 row is integer-valued (334/334, 349/349, 327/327) whereas legacy rows carry two decimals [ev_2a0e1a6df2] — the signature of integer minor units.

CONTRACT VIOLATION: DataHub documents raw.raw_orders.amount as "Order amount in MAJOR currency units as a decimal (e.g. 49.99 = $49.99). Contract v1.3: two decimal places", and documents cloudpay_v2 as a "new provider being rolled out in early August 2026". The rollout itself is expected; emitting cents is the defect [ev_b3a432a9b9].

NECESSARY AND SUFFICIENT: rescaling only the cloudpay_v2 cohort by 1/100 reproduces the committed baseline exactly — 26,557.18 / 27,383.61 / 27,373.23 revenue and 64.84 / 59.72 / 62.13 median AOV, matching baseline to the cent [ev_082bf199fc]. The invariant suite fails 7/32 tests, all downstream expressions of this one defect (max usd amount 55262, AOV median out of [30,250], revenue continuity 80-82x) [ev_c422535786].

REPAIR LAYER: normalize the cloudpay_v2 minor-unit cohort to major units in staging.stg_orders (the ingestion-contract boundary the data team owns), scoped strictly to payment_processor = 'cloudpay_v2' so healthy legacy_pos/shopgate history is untouched.

final_summary:
INCIDENT RESOLVED — 100x revenue inflation from cloudpay_v2 minor-unit amounts.

SYMPTOM
marts.exec_revenue_metric.revenue read 2,737,323.50 for kpi_day 2026-08-09 vs an expected 29,349.39 (anomaly ratio 93.3x). Baseline comparison showed a clean step change with onset exactly 2026-08-07: revenue_ratio 100.0 / 100.0 / 99.99 on 08-07/08/09 while 07-31..08-06 sat at 1.0 [ev_99f62985f4, ev_ac73812134]. Not a volume event — order_count matched baseline exactly on all three days (334/349/327); the entire distortion was per-order, with aov_median_usd inflated 100x (6483.50 vs 64.84, 5972.00 vs 59.72, 6213.00 vs 62.13) [ev_99f62985f4].

LINEAGE PATH
DataHub column-level lineage yielded a single contributing path: raw.raw_orders.amount → staging.stg_orders.amount → marts.fct_revenue.revenue_usd → marts.exec_revenue_metric.revenue, with stg_fx_rates.usd_rate as the only other branch [ev_8659030b83]. The FX branch was eliminated: usd_rate stayed stable and in-range across the onset window (CAD 0.7179–0.7198, EUR 1.0705–1.0798, GBP 1.2696–1.2746) — no 100x scaling [ev_66422a90c1]. The transforms were eliminated as the origin: stg_orders.sql only CAST amount to DOUBLE and filtered cancelled/refunded [ev_07ca87974f, ev_48dcf900b0]; fct_revenue.sql only aggregated amount * usd_rate [ev_143dc8d308]. The 100x therefore already existed in the raw feed.

ROOT CAUSE (origin isolated by cohort)
Profiling raw.raw_orders.amount segmented by payment_processor showed a complete provider cutover on 2026-08-07: through 08-06 all orders came from legacy_pos and shopgate (mean ~79–86, median ~60–70); from 08-07 onward 100% came from a new processor, cloudpay_v2, with mean 7873–8239, median 5955–6374, max 55262 [ev_46ed4fc52d]. Every cloudpay_v2 row is integer-valued — 1062/1062, first_day 2026-08-07, last_day 2026-08-09 — while legacy rows carry two decimals [ev_2a0e1a6df2, ev_1384d1d5d5]: the signature of integer minor units. DataHub documents the field as "Order amount in MAJOR currency units as a decimal (e.g. 49.99 = $49.99). Contract v1.3: two decimal places" and documents cloudpay_v2 as a provider being rolled out in early August 2026 — the rollout is expected, emitting cents is the defect [ev_b3a432a9b9]. Necessary and sufficient: rescaling only the cloudpay_v2 cohort by 1/100 reproduced the committed baseline to the cent [ev_082bf199fc]; pre-repair the invariant suite failed 7/32, all downstream expressions of this one defect [ev_c422535786].

REPAIR
pipeline/transforms/stg_orders.sql — normalized the minor-unit cohort to major units at the ingestion-contract boundary the data team owns, via CASE WHEN payment_processor = 'cloudpay_v2' THEN CAST(amount AS DOUBLE)/100.0 ELSE CAST(amount AS DOUBLE) END, with a comment documenting the contract and incident. Scoped strictly to the defective provider so legacy_pos/shopgate history is untouched; no rows dropped, filtered, or hidden (14 insertions, 1 deletion).

VERIFICATION
Warehouse rebuilt: full invariant suite 32/32 passed (was 25/32), KPI anomaly ratio 0.9327 vs the prior 93.3x. Post-repair baseline comparison shows revenue_ratio and aov_ratio of exactly 1.0 for 08-07/08/09 (26,557.18 / 27,383.61 / 27,373.23 revenue; 64.84 / 59.72 / 62.13 median AOV) with order_count unchanged, and healthy history 08-04..08-06 also still at ratio 1.0 [ev_20e5f9806d]. Shipped on branch blackbox/fix-inc_ee7f7471fb @ 018ef58113; DataHub incident marked RESOLVED (FIXED).

FOLLOW-UP FOR OWNERS: the durable fix belongs with the cloudpay_v2 integration — have the provider emit major units per contract v1.3, and add an ingestion assertion on amount decimal precision per payment_processor so a future provider cutover fails loudly instead of silently multiplying revenue.
